prediction.text:
Amazon said AWS operating income rose in 2024 mainly because of higher sales, lower payroll and related expenses, and lower depreciation and amortization. The depreciation drop came from a change in the estimated useful lives of its servers. Spending on technology infrastructure to support AWS growth partly offset these gains. AWS sales rose 19%, which Amazon attributed to increased customer usage, partly offset by pricing changes from long-term customer contracts. As context, consolidated operating income rose about 86.1% from FY2023 to FY2024. That figure is not the AWS segment change.
Amazon said the increase in AWS operating income in 2024 was primarily due to increased sales, decreased payroll and related expenses, and a reduction in depreciation and amortization expense from its change in the estimated useful lives of its servers. It said this was partially offset by spending on technology infrastructure, primarily driven by additional investments to support AWS business growth.
Amazon reported that AWS sales increased 19% in 2024 compared to the prior year. It said the growth primarily reflects increased customer usage, partially offset by pricing changes primarily driven by long-term customer contracts.
Amazon said changes in foreign exchange rates positively impacted operating income by $240 million in 2024.
For context, consolidated Amazon operating income grew about 86.1% from FY2023 ($36.85 billion) to FY2024 ($68.59 billion). This is a consolidated figure, not the AWS segment change.
